input.answer:
I can't tell you whether to buy or keep renting. That depends on your finances, timeline, and goals, and it's personal advice, which is outside what I can give. I can share one relevant data point.

New housing price index, Toronto (total: house and land), Statistics Canada table 18-10-0205:
- 2025-09: 110.4
- 2026-09: 105.0
- Change: (105.0 − 110.4) / 110.4 = −5.4 / 110.4 = −4.9%

So the index for newly built homes in Toronto fell 4.9% over the 12 months to September 2026. This covers new homes only, not resale prices. I could not retrieve a Toronto rent series in this session. The rent tables I found (46-10-0092, asking and paid rents by CMA) were not available in my data snapshot, so I can't compare rents with home prices here. For a full comparison, look at resale price data and rent data for Toronto, plus mortgage rates, property taxes, and your own budget. A fee-free rent-vs-buy calculator or a licensed mortgage professional can help with the decision.
